details:
**Juan Perón and the descamisados**
Juan Perón, a populist army officer, was elected president in 1946 and founded the Justicialist (Peronist) movement, which billed itself as a "Third Way." His working-class supporters were called the descamisados ("shirtless ones"), and their mass rally of October 17, 1945, which won his release from prison, is celebrated as "Loyalty Day." He governed from the Casa Rosada ("Pink House") in Buenos Aires.

**Dirty War and Jorge Videla**
The period of state terror (1976–1983) under the military junta of General Jorge Videla, officially called the National Reorganization Process. Security forces kidnapped, tortured, and killed thousands of suspected leftists, known as the desaparecidos ("the disappeared"). The ESMA navy school became a secret detention center, and prisoners were thrown into the sea on "death flights."

**Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo**
A protest group of women, founded in 1977, who walk around the pyramid in Buenos Aires's Plaza de Mayo every Thursday to demand information about their children who "disappeared" during the Dirty War. The Plaza de Mayo, in front of the Casa Rosada, is the country's main political square.

**Falklands War**
The 1982 war with the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands (called the Malvinas in Argentina), launched by junta leader Leopoldo Galtieri with Operation Rosario. Argentina lost the cruiser ARA General Belgrano, sunk by a British submarine, and its defeat brought down the military regime.

**Eva Perón (Evita)**
Juan Perón's second wife, born Eva Duarte, a former actress who became a champion of the descamisados. In 1947 she made the European goodwill "Rainbow Tour." She sought the vice presidency before dying of cancer in 1952, and her life inspired Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical Evita.

**Juan Manuel de Rosas and the Mazorca**
The Federalist caudillo who ruled Buenos Aires province, and through it much of Argentina, from 1829 to 1852. His Mazorca ("corncob") police terrorized the Unitarian opposition, and he fell after Justo José de Urquiza defeated him at the Battle of Caseros in 1852.

**Facundo by Domingo Faustino Sarmiento**
An 1845 book that frames Argentina's struggle as "civilization versus barbarism." It profiles the provincial caudillo Juan Facundo Quiroga, the "Tiger of the Plains," as a way of attacking Rosas. Sarmiento later served as president from 1868 to 1874.

**Isabel Perón**
Juan Perón's third wife and vice president, who succeeded him on his death in 1974, becoming the world's first female president. She was overthrown in the March 1976 coup that brought Videla's junta to power.

**Montoneros, the Triple A, and the Ezeiza massacre**
The Montoneros were left-wing Peronist guerrillas. Right-wing gunmen fired on them and other leftists at Ezeiza Airport during Perón's 1973 return from exile, and the "Triple A" (Argentine Anticommunist Alliance) death squad then killed hundreds of leftists before and into the Dirty War.

**José de San Martín**
The Argentine-born general who liberated Argentina, Chile, and Peru from Spain. In 1817 he led the Army of the Andes across the mountains to win the Battle of Chacabuco in Chile, and in 1822 he met Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil.

**Conquest of the Desert and Julio Roca**
A military campaign of the late 1870s and 1880s, led by General Julio Argentino Roca, that subjugated the Mapuche and other indigenous peoples and seized much of Patagonia. Roca then dominated politics as a leader of the "Generation of '80."

**May Revolution and the Congress of Tucumán**
The May Revolution of 1810 in Buenos Aires deposed the Spanish viceroy of the Río de la Plata and set up the first local government. The Congress of Tucumán formally declared the independence of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata in 1816.

**Hipólito Yrigoyen and the Infamous Decade**
The 1912 Sáenz Peña Law brought universal, secret male suffrage and helped Hipólito Yrigoyen of the Radical Civic Union win the presidency in 1916. His overthrow in a 1930 military coup began the "Infamous Decade" of fraud and conservative rule, which ended with the 1943 coup by the GOU officers' lodge against Ramón Castillo.

**1955 Plaza de Mayo bombing and the Revolución Libertadora**
In June 1955 navy planes bombed Perón's supporters in the Plaza de Mayo, killing hundreds. Later that year the military coup known as the Revolución Libertadora ("Liberating Revolution") ousted Perón, who went into exile until 1973.

**Adolf Eichmann (Ricardo Klement)**
The Nazi Holocaust organizer, one of many Nazis who fled to Argentina after World War II. He lived near Buenos Aires under the alias Ricardo Klement until Israeli agents captured him in 1960 and took him to Israel for trial.
